quests.followUpQuestion: Ask a coworker to send you something.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: This is a promise. When is the promise due?
quests.explanation: You heard exactly what was written. "By the end of the day" is the standard workplace way to say before people leave.
quests.prompt: I'll have the draft ready by the end of the day.
quests.sampleAnswer: I'll have the draft ready by the end of the day.
quests.followUpQuestion: Promise to finish something at a specific time.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: A describing word before "summary" shows the length expected.
quests.explanation: Short and detailed ask for very different amounts of work. "Not a full report" fits both, so only the describing word tells you what the manager wants.
quests.prompt: Our manager wants a short summary, not a full report.
quests.sampleAnswer: Our manager wants a detailed summary, not a full report.
quests.followUpQuestion: Say what your manager or teacher asked you for.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: A schedule item gives the person, then the time.
quests.explanation: Perfectly matched. "Half past ten" means ten thirty, and you'll hear it a lot at work.
quests.prompt: I have a call with a client at half past ten.
quests.sampleAnswer: I have a call with a client at half past ten.
quests.followUpQuestion: Say what's on your schedule this morning.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: A request to move a date. The length of the delay is at the end.
quests.explanation: Two days is a small favour and two weeks is a very large one. The manager would answer differently.
quests.prompt: Can we push the deadline back by two days?
quests.sampleAnswer: Can we push the deadline back by two weeks?
quests.followUpQuestion: Ask your manager or teacher for more time.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: An apology with a reason. Follow the reason.
quests.explanation: "On silent" is the natural expression for a phone that makes no sound.
quests.prompt: Sorry, I missed your message because my phone was on silent.
quests.sampleAnswer: Sorry, I missed your message because my phone was on silent.
quests.followUpQuestion: Explain why you missed a call.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: The sentence has a good result and then a contrast. What's the contrast?
quests.explanation: Nervous and tired describe very different feelings. After "although" you expect a small problem, and both fit, so you must listen.
quests.prompt: The presentation went well, although I was quite nervous.
quests.sampleAnswer: The presentation went well, although I was quite tired.
quests.followUpQuestion: Say how you felt after a presentation or test.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: A formal request ends with a day. Listen for it.
quests.explanation: It is exactly the same. "Would it be possible" is a soft, professional way to ask.
quests.prompt: Would it be possible to extend the deadline until Monday?
quests.sampleAnswer: Would it be possible to extend the deadline until Monday?
quests.followUpQuestion: Ask politely to change a deadline.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: Someone answers a phone. Follow the offer they make.
quests.explanation: "Take a message" is what a colleague offers when the person is unavailable.
quests.prompt: She's in a meeting right now, but I can take a message.
quests.sampleAnswer: She's in a meeting right now, but I can take a message.
quests.followUpQuestion: Answer the phone for a colleague who is busy.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: The job is a marketing role. Listen to how the company is described.
quests.explanation: Small and large companies feel very different to work for, and they hire in different ways.
quests.prompt: I'm applying for a marketing job at a small company.
quests.sampleAnswer: I'm applying for a marketing job at a large company.
quests.followUpQuestion: Describe the kind of company you would like to work for.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: A task must be done before a visitor comes. What is the task?
quests.explanation: Finishing the slides is creative work and printing them is a last practical step. Each takes a different amount of time.
quests.prompt: We need to print the slides before the client arrives.
quests.sampleAnswer: We need to finish the slides before the client arrives.
quests.followUpQuestion: Say what needs to be ready before a visitor comes.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: Two details are given: how long, and how the panel seemed.
quests.explanation: Nothing was altered in this one. "Seemed" is used when you describe an impression, not a fact.
quests.prompt: The interview lasted about an hour, and the panel seemed friendly.
quests.sampleAnswer: The interview lasted about an hour, and the panel seemed friendly.
quests.followUpQuestion: Describe a meeting or lesson you had, in two details.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: The instruction gives a job title. Which one?
quests.explanation: A manager and a colleague are different readers, and copying the wrong person could be embarrassing.
quests.prompt: Please copy your manager on the email.
quests.sampleAnswer: Please copy your colleague on the email.
quests.followUpQuestion: Tell someone who to add to an email.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: A problem and a request. Notice the way they're linked.
quests.explanation: Two clauses can be joined by a comma in speech because the voice pauses between them.
quests.prompt: I can't open the attachment, could you send it again?
quests.sampleAnswer: I can't open the attachment, could you send it again?
quests.followUpQuestion: Report a problem with a file and ask for help.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: A contrast: one good and one bad. Listen for the second half.
quests.explanation: "Slightly" softens the bad news, and "over budget" means it costs more than planned.
quests.prompt: The project is on schedule, but we're slightly over budget.
quests.sampleAnswer: The project is on schedule, but we're slightly over budget.
quests.followUpQuestion: Give a status update with one good and one bad point.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: The place where the work happens comes after "from".
quests.explanation: Home and office are opposite, and colleagues would arrange a meeting differently in each case.
quests.prompt: I'll be working from home on Wednesday.
quests.sampleAnswer: I'll be working from the office on Wednesday.
quests.followUpQuestion: Say where you'll work or study tomorrow.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: A question with two options. Track both halves.
quests.explanation: The recording follows the text word for word. Offering "more time" shows the speaker is willing to be flexible.
quests.prompt: Have you finished the assignment, or do you need more time?
quests.sampleAnswer: Have you finished the assignment, or do you need more time?
quests.followUpQuestion: Ask a classmate about their progress.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: A helping verb tells you how strict the advice is.
quests.explanation: Could is an option and should is a strong recommendation. A student planning an essay would take them differently.
quests.prompt: The tutor said the essay could include three examples.
quests.sampleAnswer: The tutor said the essay should include three examples.
quests.followUpQuestion: Say what you should include in your next piece of work.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: A polite way to ask someone to repeat. What didn't you catch?
quests.explanation: Name and number are both easy to mishear on a phone. Asking politely with "quite" stops it sounding rude.
quests.prompt: I'm sorry, I didn't quite catch your name just now.
quests.sampleAnswer: I'm sorry, I didn't quite catch your number just now.
quests.followUpQuestion: Ask someone to repeat something you didn't hear.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: A schedule is stated. Listen to the small word before "Monday".

quests.sampleAnswer: The team meets every Monday to review progress.
quests.followUpQuestion: Say how often you meet with a group.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: This is a request to a speaker. Notice the position of "last".
quests.explanation: Asking for an explanation is more polite than saying "I don't understand".
quests.prompt: Could you explain that last point again, please?
quests.sampleAnswer: Could you explain that last point again, please?
quests.followUpQuestion: Ask a speaker to say something again.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: The invitation includes a verb that sets the responsibility.
quests.explanation: Leading a workshop means running it, and attending means only taking part. It's a big difference in work required.
quests.prompt: My supervisor has asked me to lead the workshop.
quests.sampleAnswer: My supervisor has asked me to attend the workshop.
quests.followUpQuestion: Say what your boss or teacher asked you to do.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: A common answer to a scheduling request.
quests.explanation: It matches the text. "Get back to you" means to reply later, after you have checked.

quests.sampleAnswer: Let me check my calendar and get back to you.
quests.followUpQuestion: Respond to a request for a meeting time.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: One adjective describes how firm the deadline is.
quests.explanation: Strict and flexible are opposites. The rest of the sentence stays true, so only that word tells you whether you can relax.
quests.prompt: The deadline is strict, but only for the first draft.
quests.sampleAnswer: The deadline is flexible, but only for the first draft.
quests.followUpQuestion: Say how firm a deadline of yours is.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: An employee asks for a conversation. Listen to the topic.
quests.explanation: Schedule and salary are two very different conversations, and the manager would prepare for each in a different way.

quests.sampleAnswer: I'd like to talk to you about my salary.
quests.followUpQuestion: Ask your boss for a short talk.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.

quests.sampleAnswer: The candidate has five years of experience in design.

quests.sampleAnswer: Thanks for waiting, I'm ready to start the interview now.

quests.followUpQuestion: Suggest checking something before it is sent.
